title: Sandboxes that run syslang install Lean and cvc5 themselves, because the image carries neither
foundBy: repository owner, through the brief tasks/lean-in-the-sandbox-image.md that the syslang-playbooks session wrote: "The user has decided to put Lean and cvc5 in the image"
details:
Every sandbox that runs syslang needs Lean, because `cs-syslang validate` and every command that proves, simulates or mutates runs it through `lake`. The image has no Lean, so each campaign member installs elan and the toolchain itself. That costs a 0.6 GB download and 3 GB written to the sandbox's own disk, twice per campaign. The prover in syslang and `cs-syslang analyze` also ask the cvc5 SMT solver. Without it, more claims stay unproved.

Wanted: the base tier installs elan 4.2.4, the Lean toolchain syslang pins (leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1) and cvc5 1.4.2 on both architectures. Each download is checked against a pinned digest. The slim CI image drops all three.

A project that pins another Lean version gets it the way a Go project gets another Go. A per-user `~/.elan` links the image's toolchain, and elan downloads any other one there without `sudo`.

notes.text: A local build of all three tiers passed, from the working tree on top of 91e42fc. The Lean layer is 2837 MiB on disk and 769 MiB gzipped. The cvc5 layer is 30 MiB on disk and 11 MiB gzipped. In a Podman sandbox and in a Firecracker one, `lean` and `lake` printed 4.34.1, `cvc5 --version` printed 1.4.2, and `lean --run` ran a one-line program. With the network cut, `lake env true` exited 0. elan tries to write /opt/elan/known-projects on every call, gets EACCES and carries on. A project pinning v4.33.0 had elan install it into ~/.elan in 58 seconds, without sudo.
